feature: A see-through drawing opens the shade macOS draws it
summary: A file with see-through parts now opens on the canvas the shade macOS and a browser draw it: a line's own see-through amount, colours written see-through (rgba), and a faded group of overlapping shapes all come in right. A 30 percent shape was already right at Next defaults and still is.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. The four files are in Scripts/playtest/fixtures/svg (See-through ...svg); Scripts/playtest/see-through-svg-walk.json opens them.

try.do: File > Open 'See-through box 30.svg'. The square is mid grey (178), the grey macOS Preview shows.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open 'See-through group.svg'. Where the blue square covers the grey one it is plain pale blue; before, the grey showed through (left: before, right: now).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Look at Layers: the two squares sit in Group 1, and Group 1's Opacity is 30%. Each square inside is at 100%.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open 'See-through line.svg'. The ring is grey outside the green and dark green over it; before, it was solid black (left: before, right: now).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open 'See-through colours.svg'. The top band is pink, not solid red (left: before, right: now).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open each file in Preview beside Photonz and compare the shades.

evaluate: Does every see-through file you open look the same in Photonz as in Preview or a browser?
Is 'Group 1' a fair name for a faded group the file left unnamed, or would you rather see the file's name on it?
With a line that has its own see-through amount, the line's own colour carries it rather than the layer's Opacity. Is that where you would look to change it?
rough: No mock covers this; the yardstick is macOS's own drawing of each file, read pixel for pixel away from edges (every case within 1 level of 255).
Ask's own drawings still fade a see-through group shape by shape: only File > Open keeps such a group whole, so nothing Ask builds or animates by group name changes.

The ONNX Runtime logo (from Camtasia) still averages 7 levels off macOS at its 217 by 74 size, all of it on shape edges: its shades match and it sits about half a pixel left of macOS's drawing. That is placement, not see-through paint.
